extracted.intended_audience: West Virginians (readers, donors, sources) and others interested in nonprofit watchdog journalism in West Virginia
extracted.subtask_description: Producing nonprofit, state-focused watchdog journalism that exposes abuses of power, explains complex problems affecting West Virginians, returns repeatedly to important stories until reforms occur, and remains accessible and accountable to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — 'sustained outrage' journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: To help West Virginians improve our state by producing “sustained outrage” journalism that exposes abuses of power by government, business and other institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Borrowed from W.E. 'Ned' Chilton III: the newsroom promises to come back to stories of abuses of power, injustice, and needless harm again and again. The mission frames the organization's editorial priorities and types of stories pursued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence / follow-up reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: We’ll come back until reforms are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitment to ongoing coverage of problems — not one-off stories. Follow stories repeatedly over time, tracking whether reforms or remedies are achieved; sustain coverage until public-interest outcomes occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose abuses of power
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on stories that expose abuses of power by government, business and other institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize investigative and watchdog reporting that uncovers wrongdoing, misuse of authority, or institutional failures that harm West Virginians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to West Virginians and their communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell stories that are of great importance to West Virginians and their communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select topics with clear local impact and importance; coverage should address issues central to the state's economy, education, infrastructure, public health, and civic life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain complex problems
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear explanatory journalism that breaks down complicated policy, legal, or technical issues so ordinary readers can understand causes, consequences, and choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show how public policies affect real people
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrate how public policies affect real West Virginians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground reporting in concrete stories and examples that demonstrate policy impacts on families and communities, making abstract policy debates tangible and relatable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight scalable solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight solutions that could be scaled up to make a difference across the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond diagnosing problems, identify and explain practical solutions or reforms that have potential for wider adoption; emphasize actionable, scalable responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and directness; avoid 'he said–she said' and insider language
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t try to hide what’s really going on with a bunch of he said-she said phrasing or bureaucratic, insider language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, plain language; avoid false balance that obscures facts; avoid jargon and bureaucratic phrasing that hides accountability or confuses readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience orientation — journalism for ordinary West Virginians
rubrics_metrics.description: We do journalism for real West Virginians, not for only the political elite in Charleston.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame stories, tone, and distribution to serve the general public and community needs rather than insider or elite audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and putting reliable information into citizens' hands
rubrics_metrics.description: Putting accurate information into the hands of our citizenry is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize factual accuracy and clear presentation so citizens have the information needed to participate in civic life and make decisions for their families and communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and accountability to readers (nonprofit model)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are a nonprofit newsroom. We rely on foundations and individual donors to power our journalism. Because we rely on your support, we are accountable only to you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial independence is maintained by funding model; avoid influences from corporate owners or powerful insiders. Transparency about funding and reader accountability is implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility — no paywall; free access to journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Our stories will never be hidden behind a paywall. They will always be free to all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure public access to reporting by keeping content free; treat access to information as a public right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community engagement and sourcing (tip line)
rubrics_metrics.description: We want to hear from you. You can reach out via our tip line with story ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicit tips, story ideas, and input from readers as part of reporting process; use community-sourced leads to find and pursue investigations.
